back: The systematic examination of how work is done and how long it should take, to improve efficiency and productivity.
Recording and critically examining how a job is done now to develop a simpler, quicker or cheaper method.
Finding the time a qualified worker should take to do a job at a defined level of performance, for example by time study.
Record the present method, examine each step critically, then develop and install an improvement.
Basic time = average observed time × rating ÷ 100.
Standard time = basic time × (1 + allowance). The allowance is a percentage of the basic time.
Compares the worker's pace with a normal pace of 100. Above 100 is faster than normal; below 100 is slower.
Setting targets, planning how many workers are needed, costing jobs and comparing workers fairly.
Worker resistance, workers changing pace when timed, subjective rating, cost and skill needed, and unsuitability for creative work.
